target: Work in Q̄(u) with u transcendental and uū algebraic, so that conjugation acts on rational functions of u. H0 = Q̄ + Q̄u + Q̄ū. A 2×3 configuration in a Q̄-space V is a pair of independent families x1,x2 and y1,y2,y3 with all products x_i y_j in V. Sought in print: (a) With s real algebraic, s² = uū, F = (u/s)³ + (u/s)², the 5-dimensional conjugation-stable space W1 = H0 + Q̄F + Q̄F̄ contains no 4-dimensional H0 + Q̄w (w outside H0) carrying a 2×3 configuration, and no configuration of W1 has Möbius-in-u ratio x2/x1. (b) The same invisibility for the two-orbit space Q̄ + Q̄u + Q̄/u + Q̄g1 + Q̄g2, with g1 = α/(u−a) + β/(u+a), g2 = γ/(u−b) + δ/(u+b), a² ≠ b², and α≠β or γ≠δ. (c) Degree bound: if 1, u, 1/u lie in the span of c, ch, ch², ck, chk with h = p(u)/q(u) non-constant and coprime, then max(deg p, deg q) ≤ 2. (d) For W(λ,f) = H0 + Q̄f + Q̄f/(s+λu), with f a self-conjugate Laurent polynomial in u/s of degree k and |λ| = 1: W(λ,f) is invisible when the five numbers are free and k ≥ 3, or when k = 2 and f(−λ̄) ≠ 0. If k = 2 and f(−λ̄) = 0, then u², ū² lie in W(λ,f), which is the visible case. The configuration of W1 alone is Dia07 Th. 7(1) at v = u, w = u² + su, and does not count.

leads.quote: there exists g ∈ S such that {g, ga, . . . , gas−1 } is a basis for S
leads.derivation: My own translation: Q̄ is algebraically closed in ℂ, so with A=(x1,x2)=x1(1,a) and dim AT=4, Lemma 4 forces T=g(1,a,a²). Hence any 4-dimensional V carrying a 2×3 configuration is a progression g'(1,a,a²,a³). This is only a structural tool. It does not say that W1, the two-orbit space or W(λ,f) contains no such H0+Q̄w, and it gives neither the degree bound nor the Laurent visibility criterion. Those need a separate computation that I did not find in print.

notes:
**Verdict: no lead reaches the part not found.** I found no printed statement, or implication by a one-line derivation, of (a) invisibility of W1 or of the two-orbit space, (b) the degree ≤ 2 bound, or (c) the Laurent visibility criterion for W(λ,f). Two analogues are reported, both from the linear-Kneser/Vosper line, not the transcendence line.

**This is not a clean negative.** The forward citation chains are only partly checked, because of rate limits and blocked pages. See "Coverage" below.

**Backward from Dia07.** Its reference list has seven items: Diaz 1997 and 2004, Roy 1992, Waldschmidt 2000, 2004, 2005. Th. 7 offers just two "neighbouring families": (v, v̄)⊗(1,u,ū) and (v,vu)⊗(1,u,u²). The paper gives only non-membership in L̃ through Roy's theorem. It never asks whether a space admits another configuration or a smaller one. The notion of being invisible to four-dimensional extensions does not appear there, nor anywhere else I looked.

**Sources in the transcendence line.** The Waldschmidt 2005 papers and Diaz 2004 were keyword-scanned rather than read in full. The excerpts use stability of L̃ under conjugation only to build one configuration. I saw nothing that classifies configurations inside a space. This judgement is weaker than a full reading.

**Forward from Dia07.**
- Crossref, OpenCitations and OpenAlex each report 0 citations.
- Semantic Scholar reports 1, Waldschmidt 2005, which is an older paper and so probably a preprint-era link.
- Dia07 appears essentially uncited in these indexes, although indexes miss French-language and proceedings citations.
- zbMATH's own citation list could not be opened.

**Forward from Roy 1992.** The Semantic Scholar titles (19, latest 2022) are Iwasawa and p-adic applications or Waldschmidt surveys, with no space-theoretic classification. OpenAlex counts 21 but its list was rate-limited.

**After 5 October 2026.** arXiv title and abstract searches through 8 November show only two abstracts mentioning six exponentials: Pańkowski (2610.41600) and Neroli (2610.10469). Both merely use the theorem, or mention it, in other fields. Nothing concerned Diaz's conjecture, L̃ or conjugation. arXiv search covers titles and abstracts only, so a recent paper citing Dia07 only in its body would be missed.

**The closest actual mathematics.** BSZ Lemma 4 gives, over any base algebraically closed in the extension, that dim(1,a)T = dim T + 1 forces T to be a progression in a. With BSZ Theorem 2 this yields, by my own translation, that a 4-dimensional V carrying a 2×3 configuration is g'(1,a,a²,a³). That is the general shape behind a four-dimensional extension carrying a configuration. It does not decide whether a given W contains such an extension. Excluding it for W1, the two-orbit space and W(λ,f) is a calculation with specific rational functions, and that calculation is what I did not find. So I record this as analogue only. A verifier may still want it as an independent reference for the progression step, if the blueprint proves that step from scratch; I did not look at how the blueprint does it.

**Why a print find looks unlikely (my opinion, not evidence).**
- The statements are lemma-level computations about specific spaces, motivated by a question that the printed sources do not pose.
- For the degree bound I sketched an elimination: eliminating k gives a relation among 1, u, 1/u over Q̄(h), and this constrains [Q̄(u):Q̄(h)]. I did not complete the case analysis. It suggests why the result would appear at most as an unremarked lemma, under no searchable name.
- This agrees with the "routine" class in the target file.

**Coverage.**
- Stopped at about 15 minutes of the 30-minute box (15:33 to about 15:48 by the clock). Further index retries kept returning 429, and the remaining chains need a rate-limit window, not more queries.
- Unchecked: the zbMATH citing list for Dia07, OpenAlex forward lists, forward citations of Diaz 2004 (my DOI guess was wrong) and of Waldschmidt 2005.
- Not read: BCZ Theorem 6.3, Couvreur-Zémor 2024, Wessel 2024 in depth. They treat S², not pairs, and would at most add analogues.
- The Dasgupta-Kakde and Wessel entries rest on search-tool summaries, not on my reading of the sources.
- Formulas in BSZ and BCZ come from text layers and were not checked against page images. Lemma 4 is short and read clearly.
- Excluded as instructed: Lean repositories, the blueprint, prove2.me, formalpedia.
